items.difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the Compactness Theorem for propositional logic at source lines 508-512: a set of sentences is satisfiable exactly when every finite subset is. The author proof (514-519) is a three-link chain of equivalences, and each link demands a different tool: satisfiability is traded for consistency through the completeness theorem and its converse through soundness, both proved earlier in the same unit, while the middle link trades consistency of an infinite set for consistency of a finite subset, which needs the structural fact that a derivation has finitely many open assumptions. None of the links is a definition unpacking alone, and the reader has to see which direction of which theorem each step uses, so the unit is more than a one-line consequence of the definitions.
